knowledge_point.title: Differentiating an Exponential Function with a Nonlinear Exponent

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y=e^{u},\,u=-3{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-4.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=e^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-9{x}^{2}-4x.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\ & =e^{u}\cdot (-9{x}^{2}-4x) \\ & =(-9{x}^{2}-4x)e^{u} \\ & =\left(- 9 x^{2} - 4 x\right) e^{- 3 x^{3} - 2 x^{2} - 4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=-2$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|_{x=-2} & =(-9{x}^{2}-4x)e^{-3{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-4}|_{x=-2} \\ & =(-9(-2)^{2}-4(-2))e^{-3(-2)^{3}-2(-2)^{2}-4} \\ & =-28\cdot e^{12} \\ & =- 28 e^{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\ & =e^{u}\cdot (-9{x}^{2}+4x) \\ & =(-9{x}^{2}+4x)e^{u} \\ & =\left(- 9 x^{2} + 4 x\right) e^{- 3 x^{3} + 2 x^{2} + 4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=2$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|_{x=2} & =(-9{x}^{2}+4x)e^{-3{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}+4}|_{x=2} \\ & =(-9(2)^{2}+4(2))e^{-3(2)^{3}+2(2)^{2}+4} \\ & =-28\cdot e^{-12} \\ & =- \frac{28}{e^{12}}.\end{aligned}
